# 14.2 arm campaign — the loop, and the record

The three-arm comparison (`baseline`, `doctrine`, `conductor`) is not run once. It is run,
stopped when the measurement is found to be wrong, fixed, and run again from nothing. This
page is the protocol for that loop and the running record of every pass through it.

It follows the shape of [`13.2-findings-register.md`](13.2-findings-register.md) deliberately:
stable IDs, the observation verbatim, what it falsifies, and **a prediction written down before
the fix** — then that prediction checked against the next run. The prediction is the part that
matters. A register without predictions records that you went in a circle; a register with them
tells you at the next run whether you did.

---

## 1. What stops a run, and what does not

Three different things go wrong in this campaign, and only one of them is a reason to stop.

| Class | Meaning | On discovery |
|-------|---------|--------------|
| **Harness defect** | The measurement is wrong. The numbers being produced do not mean what the scoreboard says they mean. | **Stop the run immediately.** Every cell after this point is wasted. |
| **Arm defect** | An arm behaves badly — bad scope, wasted turns, a wrong trajectory. | **Do not stop.** This is the product. Record it, batch the fix into the next epoch. |
| **Model quality** | The model wrote poor or wrong code. | **Never stop.** This is the entire thing being measured. |

The distinction is load-bearing. If every bad result stops the run, the campaign never leaves
T0 — and T3/T4 is the only tier where the conductor's overhead could plausibly pay for itself,
which is the question the campaign exists to answer. Stop when the data is **invalid**, not when
it is **unflattering**.

A useful test for which class you are in: *if this were left alone, would the final report state
something false?* Harness defects make the report lie. Arm defects make the report unflattering,
which is a result.

## 2. Two run sizes

A full run is 23 tasks x 3 arms = 69 cells. At the rates observed in epoch 1 — the two
non-baseline arms hitting the 30-minute wall on the *cheapest* task in the set — that is
twenty-plus hours. Making that the unit of iteration means a defect found at task 2 costs a day
to rediscover.

So there are two:

- **Probe** — one task per tier (T0, T1, T2, T4), 4 tasks x 3 arms = 12 cells. This is the
  epoch gate. Run it after every fix. Its job is to answer "is the harness sound and does each
  arm reach an ending", not "which arm is better".
- **Full** — all 69 cells. This is the measurement. Run it only when a probe comes back with no
  harness defects.

Both are `run_and_watch.py` with different constants; `TASKS` and `TIERS` already exist for
exactly this and no code has to change to switch between them.

## 3. Every epoch starts from nothing

Already true, and worth knowing so nobody builds machinery for it:

- Each cell gets a **fresh git repo**, re-created rather than cleaned, with one seed commit.
- Each cell gets a **hermetic home** — `HOME` and every `XDG_*` isolated — so no session
  history, cache or credential crosses between cells or between epochs.
- `RESULTS_DIR = None` mints a **fresh timestamped directory** per launch, so no epoch can
  silently reuse a previous epoch's finished cells.

The one thing that carries across epochs is the thing that should: the code, and this page.

## 4. What an epoch records

Kept deliberately small, because a template nobody fills in by epoch four is worse than none.

1. **Epoch number, date, and the git SHA.** Without the SHA, "epoch 3" is not a recoverable
   state and nothing here can be re-derived.
2. **The served configuration** — model, `--parallel`, `--ctx-size`, and the resulting per-slot
   window. These are inputs that change results and do not live in the code.
3. **What changed since the last epoch**, by defect ID.
4. **The scoreboard** — generated from the result JSON, never hand-written. Hand-typed tables
   drift from the data they claim to summarize.
5. **New defects**, with IDs, following the register format below.
6. **Status transitions of existing defects.** This is the cycle detector. A defect that reads
   `open -> fixed -> open` is a cycle, and it is visible at a glance instead of buried in prose.

## 5. Documentation detects cycles. Tests prevent them.

The most important line on this page.

A register cannot stop a regression. It can only tell you, afterwards, that one happened. If the
loop leans on this document alone, it will faithfully and accurately record itself going in
circles.

So: **every harness defect fixed lands with a test that fails without the fix.** That is already
the repository's standing rule — "New behaviour arrives with a test that fails without it" — and
it is the actual anti-cycle mechanism. This page carries the ones a test cannot: emergent
behaviour, trajectory changes, cost, and anything whose failure mode is "the model did something
different this time".

---

# Defect register

Status is one of `open`, `fixed`, or `reopened`. `reopened` is never overwritten — a defect that
returns keeps its history, because that history is the finding.

| ID | Class | Summary | Status |
|----|-------|---------|--------|
| D01 | harness | A timed-out cell is never scored, so "could not do it" and "would not stop" are the same number | fixed (epoch 2) |
| D02 | harness | The arms do not get equal usable context; doctrine's prompt takes 42% of the window | fixed (epoch 2) |
| D03 | arm | The conductor's testScope aims the testWriter at the graded suite | open |
| D04 | arm | The conductor spends 37% of the budget classifying and never reaches an implementer | open |
| D05 | arm | The orchestrator attempts an illegal decompose on a run it just classified trivial | open |
| D06 | harness | `.conductor/config.json` is seeded into arms whose comment claims they never read it | open |

---

## D01 — a timed-out cell is never scored

- **Class:** harness. Invalidates data. Stops the run.
- **Observed (epoch 1, `doctrine/slugify-ts`):** recorded `outcome: "timeout"`, `passed: false`.
  The work tree was copied out and the hidden gauge materialized against it by hand:

  ```
  gauge     5 tests, 5 pass, 0 fail
  visible   1 test,  1 pass, 0 fail
  ```

  The arm had a fully correct solution in hand when the clock expired. The same run also
  authored `tests/slugify.test.ts` with nine cases and confirmed it red before editing `src/`.
- **Mechanism:** in `run_cell`, `if run_outcome.timed_out or run_outcome.spawn_error:` scores
  immediately and skips `materialize_files(work, task.hidden_files)` entirely. The tree is never
  measured.
- **Falsifies:** the scoreboard's `passed` column as a statement about capability. A timed-out
  cell holding a perfect solution and one holding a wrecked repository record identically.
- **Why it stops a run:** both non-baseline arms timed out on the cheapest task in the set. A
  full run under this defect produces a report saying doctrine and conductor solved nothing,
  which is false.
- **Prediction (before fix):** with the tree scored on timeout and the timeout recorded as a
  separate axis from the gauge verdict, `doctrine/slugify-ts` reports gauge-pass with
  `timedOut: true`, and `conductor/slugify-ts` reports gauge-fail with `timedOut: true`. The two
  cells stop being the same number.

## D02 — the arms do not get equal usable context

- **Class:** harness. A confound in the experiment's design.
- **Observed (epoch 1):**

  ```
  doctrine-prompt.md              55,254 bytes   ~13.8k tokens
  per-slot context limit                         32,768 tokens
  ```

  The window is `--ctx-size 196608` divided across `--parallel 6`. The doctrine arm pays ~13.8k
  of that on every request before the task is read; baseline pays approximately none.
- **Consequence:** three full compaction cycles in the `doctrine/slugify-ts` transcript against
  zero in `baseline/slugify-ts`. Two consecutive cycles resumed on the same instruction:

  ```
  - About to author failing test file `tests/slugify.test.ts` covering: dash-join, run-collapse...
  - About to author failing test file `tests/slugify.test.ts` using the visible test's node:test style
  - About to edit `src/slugify.ts` from the current trim/lowercase body to the chosen regex implementation
  ```

  Each summary is itself ~1.5-2k tokens and re-enters the window, so every cycle leaves less
  room than the last.
- **Falsifies:** the premise that the arms differ only in guidance. They differ in usable
  working memory by more than 2x, and the T0 tier — which exists to price ceremony overhead —
  is where that difference bites hardest, because there is no real work to amortize it against.
- **Prediction (before fix):** served at `--parallel 2` (98,304 per slot), `doctrine/slugify-ts`
  shows **zero** compaction cycles, finishes inside the T0 budget, and reports gauge-pass
  without a timeout.

## D03 — the conductor's testScope aims the testWriter at the graded suite

- **Class:** arm. This is a result, not a reason to stop.
- **Observed (epoch 1, `conductor/slugify-ts`), the testWriter sub-session's own words:**

  > Test file written to `tests/visible.test.ts` (the only path in testScope).

  Final tree: `src/slugify.ts` untouched, five failing cases appended to the graded suite,
  gauge 0/5, visible 2/6. The seed's own green suite was left red.
- **Why it happens:** the task requires `tests/visible.test.ts` keep passing; TDD requires a red
  test; the derived testScope offered only the graded file. The two requirements collide and the
  conductor resolves the collision by breaking the graded suite.
- **The contrast that makes this a defect rather than an impossibility:** the `doctrine` arm hit
  the identical conflict and reasoned its way out unprompted —

  > TDD doctrine: prefer new test file per item (`tests/slugify.test.ts`); graded suite only
  > runs `visible.test.ts`, so new file documents red->green but is not part of the graded run.

  Doctrine got this right by thinking. Conductor got it wrong by configuration.

## D04 — the conductor never reaches an implementer

- **Class:** arm.
- **Observed (epoch 1, `conductor/slugify-ts`), from the run journal:**

  ```
   0.0 -  2.4 min   startup, before the first wave
   2.4 -  8.7 min   classify sub-session            375s
   8.7 - 10.9 min   skeptic cross-check             135s
  10.9 - 11.4 min   orchestrator attempts conductor_decompose, refused
  11.4 - 13.3 min   recovering from the refusal     111s
  13.3 - 17.2 min   testWriter                      234s
  17.2 - 18.0 min   red detected, item -> RED
  18.0 - 26.3 min   reviewer 1 of 3                 497s
  26.3 - 28.0 min   reviewer 2 of 3                 100s
  28.0 - 30.0 min   reviewer 3 never returned; wall clock expired
  ```

  Eleven minutes — 37% of the budget — established that a four-line string function is trivial.
  Three reviewers were then dispatched concurrently, on 5,726-character prompts, to review a
  five-case test file. No implementer ran. No line of `src/` was written.
- **The structural reading:** the conductor makes roughly seven **sequential** model round-trips
  before an implementer starts. Against cloud latency each is seconds and invisible. Against a
  local 27B each is two to eight minutes, so the orchestration alone exceeds the whole T0 budget
  before any code exists. The architecture is priced for cheap model calls and is deployed where
  calls are expensive.
- **Not a stop:** this is exactly what the T0 tier was built to measure, and it measured it.

## D05 — the orchestrator attempts an illegal decompose

- **Class:** arm. **The guard worked**, and that is the finding worth keeping.
- **Observed (epoch 1, `conductor/slugify-ts`, journal seq 33):**

  ```
  refused  conductor_decompose: illegal run transition EXECUTING->DECOMPOSED;
           from EXECUTING the legal successor(s): REPORTED, TRIVIAL_DONE (§3.1)
  ```

  The orchestrator reached for `conductor_decompose` on a run it had itself classified `trivial`
  one step earlier, with the skeptic agreeing. The FSM refused it.
- **Reading:** a guard catching a real model error is the system working. A guard *needing* to
  catch it means the orchestrator's prompt is not steering the trivial path. Recovery from the
  refusal then cost a further 111 seconds.
- Recorded because a guard that fires is evidence about the prompt, not proof the guard is
  correct — see the standing rule about reproducing a guard's computation before trusting it.

## D06 — a seeded file the no-plugin arms were assumed not to read

- **Class:** harness. Minor; does not invalidate data. Batch it.
- **Observed:** `run_cell` seeds `.conductor/config.json` into every arm's tree deliberately, so
  the three arms are compared on an identical tree. The comment defending that ends:

  > The arms with no plugin never read the file.

  The `doctrine` arm read it on `slugify-ts` and carried it in its working inventory:

  ```
  - `.conductor/config.json`: verify command + behavioralPaths/git config.
  ```
- **Falsifies:** that comment, as written. The arms never *act* on the file, which is what the
  design cares about — but they spend a read and context on machinery they do not have, and on
  a T0 task that is a measurable slice of the run.
- Either narrow the comment to "never act on it", or withhold the file from the arms with no
  plugin and accept the differing file listing.

# Epoch log

## Epoch 1 — 2026-08-22

- **SHA:** `9934283` (`run_and_watch: bring the model up for the run and take it down after`)
- **Served:** `qwen3.8-27b`, `--ctx-size 196608`, `--parallel 6` -> **32,768 per slot**
- **Run:** full (69 cells) — **stopped after 4** on D01
- **Results:** `.data/benchmark/watch/20260822-024521/`
- **Changed since last epoch:** nothing; this is the first.

### Scoreboard

| task | arm | outcome | wall | tokens | gauge | visible |
|------|-----|---------|------|--------|-------|---------|
| slugify-ts | baseline | pass | 7.0 min | 116k | 5/5 | 1/1 |
| slugify-ts | doctrine | timeout | 30.0 min | 232k | **5/5** | 1/1 |
| slugify-ts | conductor | timeout | 30.0 min | 305k | 0/5 | **2/6** |
| retry-ts | baseline | pass | 5.1 min | 72k | 5/5 | pass |
| retry-ts | doctrine | *killed by the stop* | — | — | — | — |

Gauge columns for the two timed-out cells were taken by hand, against copies of the work trees,
because D01 means the harness never took them.

### Read

Baseline is doing well and cheaply: two for two, averaging six minutes and 94k tokens, no wasted
ceremony, and on `retry-ts` it reset the audit array with `usedDelays.length = 0` rather than
reassigning a `const` export — a detail that separates a passing test from a working module.

Doctrine is doing the **best engineering of the three** and scoring worst. It ran genuine TDD on
`slugify-ts`, nine cases, confirmed red before editing. It lost to D02, not to the task.

Conductor is the only arm that left a repository worse than the seed. Its classification stage
and its FSM guard both worked correctly and visibly; everything downstream of them did not
finish.

### Defects raised

D01, D02, D03, D04, D05, D06 — all `open`.

### Stopped because

D01. Both non-baseline arms timed out on the cheapest task in the set, and under D01 a full run
would have reported that they solved nothing. That report would have been false.

---

## Epoch 2 — 2026-08-22

- **Served:** `qwen3.8-27b`, **3 slots x 65,536 per slot** = 196,608 total (unchanged total; the
  per-slot window doubles at no cost in KV cache)
- **Run:** probe — one task per tier, 4 tasks x 3 arms = 12 cells
- **Changed since epoch 1:** D01, D02

### D01 — fixed

`run_cell` measures the tree however the cell ended. A timeout no longer skips
`materialize_files`; the hidden suite runs and its verdict is recorded on its own axis.
Delivery and correctness became two fields rather than one:

- `outcome` / `passed` — unchanged in meaning. A timeout is still a timeout and still not a
  pass. Nothing in the aggregation moved.
- `timedOut` — bool.
- `gauge` — `{ran, passed, exitCode}`, the hidden suite's verdict on the final tree.

The gauge's own duration is deliberately kept out of `wallClockMs`: the clock was already
spent, and measurement taken after the fact is not the cell's cost. A cell that never spawned
records `gauge.ran: false` rather than a verdict on the untouched seed.

The report's timeouts section now names which of the two happened, per cell:

```
- <cellId> (tree PASSES the hidden suite - overran with a correct solution in hand)
- <cellId> (tree fails the hidden suite)
```

**Tests:** `test_timeout_still_measures_the_tree`, `test_spawn_error_measures_nothing`,
`test_report_separates_overran_from_wrong`. Verified red against epoch 1's code — one failure
and two errors — then green.

### D02 — fixed

Slots 6 -> 3 and per-slot window 32,768 -> 65,536, via `SERVE_SLOTS` and
`SERVE_PER_SLOT_CONTEXT` in `run_and_watch.py`, passed to `serve.py` as `--max-readers` and
`--ctx`. The product is unchanged, so the KV cache is unchanged; three slots still covers the
conductor's observed three-reviewer fan-out without serializing it.

`opencode_usable_window()` was added to `conductor_wiring.py` — the compaction threshold
existed only as a comment, and D02 needed it as a value.

Usable window per arm: **24,576 -> 49,152**. The doctrine packs go from 56% of it to 28%.

**Tests:** `test_doctrine_prompt_leaves_room_to_work` pins the packs under a third of the
usable window and requires the arm have more room to work in than its own prompt occupies;
`test_usable_window_follows_the_served_slot` pins the threshold to the served slot. Both read
`SERVE_PER_SLOT_CONTEXT` out of `run_and_watch.py` rather than a constant of their own, so the
served window and the invariant cannot drift apart — which is the failure D02 *is*. Verified
red at epoch 1's window: `13730 tokens of a 24576-token usable window (56%)`.
